title: Sending a Parcel at the Post Office
situation: You go to the 우체국 to mail a box of clothes to a friend in another city and ask about price and delivery time.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 다음 분이요. 어떤 거 보내시겠어요?
lines.en: Next, please. What would you like to send?
lines.note: 다음 분이요 = 'next person, please' (calling the next customer); 보내시겠어요? = honorific 'would you like to send?'

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 이 택배 하나 보내려고요. 부산으로요.
lines.en: I'd like to send this parcel. To Busan.
lines.note: 택배 = parcel/courier delivery; -(으)려고요 = 'I'm planning to ~'; -(으)로 marks the destination

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 안에 뭐 들었어요? 깨지는 물건 있어요?
lines.en: What's inside? Anything breakable?
lines.note: 뭐 들었어요? = what's in it?; 깨지는 물건 = breakable item (깨지다 = to break)

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 옷이랑 책 몇 권이요. 깨지는 건 없어요.
lines.en: Some clothes and a few books. Nothing breakable.
lines.note: -(이)랑 = and (casual); 몇 권 = a few (counter 권 for books)

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 그럼 무게부터 잴게요. 여기 위에 올려 주세요.
lines.en: Then let me weigh it first. Please put it up here.
lines.note: 무게를 재다 = to weigh; -부터 = starting with; 올리다 = to put up/place on

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 얼마 나와요? 그리고 부산까지 며칠 걸려요?
lines.en: How much does it come to? And how many days to Busan?
lines.note: 얼마 나와요? = how much does it come out to?; 며칠 걸려요? = how many days does it take? (며칠, never 몇일)

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 육천 원이고요, 일반으로 보내면 보통 이틀이면 도착해요. 더 빨리 받으시려면 익일특급도 있어요.
lines.en: It's 6,000 won, and with regular shipping it usually arrives in two days. If you want it sooner, there's next-day express too.
lines.note: -이고요 = 'it is ~, and' (polite linking); 일반 = regular; -(이)면 = if/when; 익일특급 = next-day express; -(으)려면 = if you want to ~

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 그냥 일반으로 할게요. 송장은 어떻게 써요?
lines.en: I'll just go with regular. How do I fill out the waybill?
lines.note: 일반 = regular (vs. express); 송장 = waybill/shipping label; -(으)ㄹ게요 = I'll ~ (deciding)

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 여기 받는 분 성함하고 주소, 연락처 적어 주세요.
lines.en: Write the recipient's name, address, and phone number here.
lines.note: 받는 분 = the recipient; 성함 = honorific for name; 적다 = to write down

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 다 썼어요. 나중에 어디까지 왔는지 조회돼요?
lines.en: I'm done writing. Can I track where it is later?
lines.note: 어디까지 왔는지 = how far it has come; 조회되다 = to be trackable / able to be looked up

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 네, 이 운송장 번호로 인터넷에서 조회하시면 돼요.
lines.en: Yes, you can track it online with this tracking number.
lines.note: 운송장 번호 = tracking number; -(으)로 = by means of; -(으)시면 돼요 = you just need to ~

tip: Bring your own box if you can — the post office sells boxes (우체국 박스) but charges for them. Say 일반 (regular) for the standard rate or 익일특급 for next-day express. Always keep the 운송장 번호 (tracking number) so you can check delivery status on the 우체국택배 app or website. For breakable items, ask them to add 파손주의 (fragile) tape.

title: Signing Up at the Gym
situation: You visit a neighborhood 헬스장 to sign up and ask about membership length, the locker, and PT sessions.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 안녕하세요. 등록 상담 받으러 오셨어요?
lines.en: Hello. Are you here to ask about signing up?
lines.note: 등록 = registration/sign-up; 상담 받다 = to get a consultation; -(으)러 오다 = to come in order to ~

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 네, 헬스장 회원권 알아보려고요.
lines.en: Yes, I'd like to look into a gym membership.
lines.note: 헬스장 = gym (everyday word); 회원권 = membership; 알아보다 = to look into

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 얼마나 다니실 생각이세요? 기간별로 가격이 달라요.
lines.en: How long are you thinking of attending? The price varies by period.
lines.note: 다니다 = to attend/go regularly; 기간별로 = by period; 다르다 = to be different

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 세 달 끊으면 한 달에 얼마예요?
lines.en: If I sign up for three months, how much per month?
lines.note: 끊다 = to buy/sign up for (a pass); 한 달에 = per month

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 세 달은 한 달에 오만 원이에요. 육 개월은 더 싸요.
lines.en: Three months is 50,000 won a month. Six months is cheaper.
lines.note: 육 개월 = six months; 더 싸요 = it's cheaper (싸다 = to be cheap)

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 운동복이랑 수건도 빌릴 수 있어요?
lines.en: Can I rent workout clothes and a towel too?
lines.note: 운동복 = workout clothes; 수건 = towel; 빌리다 = to borrow/rent; -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 = can

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 운동복 대여는 한 달에 만 원 추가예요. 락커는 무료고요.
lines.en: Clothing rental is 10,000 won extra a month. The locker is free.
lines.note: 대여 = rental; 추가 = extra/additional; 락커 = locker; 무료 = free of charge

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: PT도 받고 싶은데, 한 번 받아 볼 수 있어요?
lines.en: I'd also like to do PT — can I try one session?
lines.note: PT(피티) = personal training; 받다 = to receive (a session); -아/어 보다 = to try ~ing

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 그럼 무료 체험 한 번 잡아 드릴게요. 결제는 카드로 하시겠어요?
lines.en: Then I'll set up one free trial for you. Will you pay by card?
lines.note: 무료 체험 = free trial; 잡다 = to book/arrange (here 'set up'); 결제 = payment; -(으)시겠어요? = polite 'will you ~?'

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 네, 카드요. 혹시 중간에 환불도 돼요?
lines.en: Yes, by card. By the way, can I get a refund partway through?
lines.note: 중간에 = in the middle/partway; 환불 = refund; -도 돼요? = is ~ also allowed?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 남은 기간만큼은 환불 가능해요. 여기 신청서 작성해 주세요.
lines.en: You can be refunded for the remaining period. Please fill out this form here.
lines.note: 남은 기간만큼 = as much as the remaining period; 신청서 = application form; 작성하다 = to fill out

tip: Longer plans (육 개월, 일 년) cut the monthly price a lot, but only commit long-term once you're sure you'll keep going. Ask about 운동복 대여 (clothing rental) and 락커 (locker) — some gyms include them, others charge extra. By law, gyms must refund the unused portion if you cancel, though they may deduct a small penalty, so keep your receipt and check the 환불 규정 (refund policy) before signing.
